root_cause.text: The RDS info-collection helpers reused an uninitialized on-stack per-item buffer and copied the entire struct to user space even when the IB connection visitors only partially populated it, leaking stale stack data from `rds_for_each_conn_info()`/`rds_walk_conn_path_info()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `memset(buffer, 0, item_len);` before calling the visitors in both `rds_for_each_conn_info()` and `rds_walk_conn_path_info()`, and the CVE text states that `rds_ib_conn_info_visitor()`/`rds6_ib_conn_info_visitor()` leave several fields and an alignment hole unwritten when `rds_connection` is not `RDS_CONN_UP`, which are then `memcpy_to_user()`'d via `rds_info_copy()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero the per-item info buffer before visitor population to prevent stack data leakage to user space.
intent_record.what: A memset(buffer, 0, item_len) call was inserted immediately before invoking visitor(conn, buffer) inside rds_for_each_conn_info(), along with a comment explaining that the per-item buffer is zeroed before each visitor call.
intent_record.how: Each iteration now starts with a cleared buffer, so any fields the visitor does not populate, including padding bytes, are initialized to zero before the data is copied to user space. This prevents accidental leakage of stale stack contents through rds_info_copy().

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero the per-item RDS path info buffer before visitor writes to prevent stack memory leakage via info copy.
intent_record.what: The code now calls `memset(buffer, 0, item_len);` before invoking `visitor(cp, buffer)` in `rds_walk_conn_path_info()`, along with a new comment explaining that the per-item buffer must be zeroed to avoid leaking uninitialized stack bytes, including padding, through `rds_info_copy()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, each item buffer is cleared before the visitor fills it, ensuring any fields or alignment padding left unwritten contain zeroes instead of stale stack data. This prevents accidental exposure of kernel stack contents when the buffer is later copied out.

candidates.rationale: This call passes an on-stack per-item buffer to the visitor without first initializing it, so if the visitor only partially fills the struct, stale stack contents can later be copied out.
This is the analogous unchecked visitor invocation for path info; the buffer is reused uninitialized, enabling leakage of uninitialized stack data when the populated struct is copied to user space.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call hands an on-stack per-item buffer to the visitor without prior initialization, so any fields the visitor does not overwrite can retain stale stack data that later gets copied to user space.
This analogous visitor call reuses an uninitialized stack buffer for path info collection, allowing partially populated structs to leak uninitialized stack contents when copied out.
